Because direct scientific literature could not be retrieved due to an API error, this explanation relies on established biological and pharmacological principles. 

Gefitinib is an orally active, small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that selectively and reversibly binds to the adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-binding pocket within the intracellular tyrosine kinase domain of the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR). In non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), particularly in tumors harboring activating *EGFR* mutations (such as exon 19 deletions or the L858R point mutation), EGFR is constitutively active and drives oncogenic proliferation and survival. By competitively inhibiting ATP binding, gefitinib blocks EGFR autophosphorylation and shuts down downstream pro-survival signaling cascades (including the MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt pathways), thereby inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in NSCLC cells.
